clue.text: Fairness, possibly, of unembellished letter

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of the word before it might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Asking whether beauty can be found in a plain, unadorned letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of FAIRNESS. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface without serifs has letters lacking the small decorative strokes, so its letters are plain.

clue.text: Poisonous element when I'm embraced by triumvir

indicators.note: being embraced by something means sitting inside it, so the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: Mark Antony was one of Rome's Second Triumvirate
I'm gives its letters as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler hugging someone turns out to be deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: The triumvir is Mark Antony, who ruled Rome alongside Octavian and Lepidus. 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemical element with symbol Sb is a toxic metalloid, so it is a poisonous element.

clue.text: Take deep breath before walking or playing for the first time

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: to sigh is to take a long deep audible breath
treading is walking, setting the feet down

explanation.surface: Advice to inhale deeply before setting off, or before a first performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walking' looks like part of the definition's picture, but it supplies letters; 'or' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight-reading is performing music at first sight from a score, without rehearsal.

clue.text: Warranted postponement of piano reverie arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts items into a new order, so the letters here are reordered

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A musical arrangement of a dreamy piano piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges P plus REVERIE. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve is an official delay or cancellation of a punishment, granted by warrant.

clue.text: Puck is dropped in it, show being cancelled

parts.note: to show one's face is to appear, so face can mean show
an event called off is cancelled

explanation.surface: A TV show being axed, with a mischievous sprite like Shakespeare's Puck dropped from it.
explanation.walkthrough: Puck looks like the Shakespeare sprite but is an ice-hockey puck. 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In ice hockey play starts with the official dropping the puck between two opposing players.

clue.text: A train off the rails in the capital

indicators.note: a train off the rails is derailed and disordered, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A derailment in a nation's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off the rails' rearranges A TRAIN. 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirana is the capital city of Albania.

clue.text: Mahler's third without the opening longing?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed 'Mahler's third without the opening longing? (4)': longing gives ITCH, but no reading of 'Mahler's third without the opening' builds ITCH with every word used (ICH outside T leaves 'third' unexplained).
annotationWithheld.clue: Mahler's third without the opening longing?

clue.text: Kind of screen role that turns up and lets actor down

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the pieces from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a rood screen separates the nave from the chancel in a church
an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: Describing a stage role that springs up and then lets its actor fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that turns up' reverses ROOD + PART as a whole, giving TRAPDOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage trapdoor opens in the floor, lowering a performer below the boards.

clue.text: He pictured life in Pluto

parts.note: a Disney artist drew a cartoon dog called Pluto and brought him to life frame by frame

explanation.walkthrough: Pluto looks like the planet or god of the underworld, but is Mickey Mouse's dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon artist gives drawn characters the appearance of movement and life.

clue.text: Sabbath — day in Germany that is all male

parts.note: Tag is German for day

explanation.surface: Observing that a German Sunday is a men-only affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is a link. A stag party or night is for men only.
explanation.definitionFit: Stag as an adjective means for men only, as in a stag party.

clue.text: Show skill on Hampshire's turns

indicators.note: turns suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Displaying talent on the bends of a Hampshire road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' rearranges ON plus HAMPSHIRES, the possessive apostrophe giving no letter. Hampshire is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsemanship is the skill of riding, displayed at an equestrian show.

clue.text: People out and about?

parts.note: people who are out cold, asleep, yet walking about at night

explanation.definitionFit: Somnambulists move around while unconscious, so they are out yet about.

clue.text: Pursue career

definitions.meaning: to chase, as hounds chase a hare

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to hunt game with hounds, and to run or flow swiftly.

clue.text: Passion shown by officer-type in such dancing?

parts.note: a flame is a burning passion
an NCO is a non-commissioned officer, a kind of officer

explanation.surface: A fiery sergeant showing ardour on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown by' and 'in' are links. Flamenco is a passionate Spanish dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is a fiery Andalusian dance style, so it is a kind of dancing.

clue.text: Pirouetted and minced round yard

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: grated food is minced into small bits

explanation.surface: A dancer spinning and mincing about the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: Minced looks like a way of walking, but means grated. 'round' puts GRATED around Y. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To pirouette is to spin on one foot, so it means to have turned in circles.

clue.text: Greylag?

parts.note: a greylag is a goose, a bird, while a lag is a convict and an old grey one has done long time

explanation.definitionFit: A habitual criminal is called an old lag; a grey lag suggests a jailed bird.

clue.text: One who buys a second receptacle

parts.note: a hopper is a funnel-shaped container for grain or coal

explanation.definitionFit: A customer at a store is someone purchasing goods.

clue.text: Gas layer about dry — go another way

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hen goes round the other piece

parts.note: a hen is a layer of eggs

indicators.note: putting the letters another way means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A layer of gas over dry ground, told to take a different route.
explanation.walkthrough: Layer looks like a stratum but is an egg-laying hen; 'another way' scrambles the next two words, and 'about' wraps the bird round that result.
explanation.definitionFit: The lightest element, number one on the periodic table, is a gas.

clue.text: How part of plan is shown up

definitions.text: How part of plan is shown up

parts.words: How part of plan is shown up
parts.note: an architect's drawings include a side view, the elevation, which shows the building raised up

explanation.definitionFit: An architectural elevation is a vertical view, part of a building's plans, and elevated means raised up.

clue.text: Drink made from the nettle?

definitions.meaning: a cocktail of brandy and white crème de menthe
a plant that stings, so it can be called one that stings

explanation.definitionFit: A brandy-and-crème-de-menthe cocktail has this name, and a nettle is a plant that stings.

clue.text: Bowing and twirling the baton is easy at first

indicators.note: twirling spins the baton round, so its letters are turned into a new order
at first takes just the opening letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Bowing to the crowd and spinning a baton look simple at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twirling' rearranges BATON + IS + E, the E coming from 'easy at first'. 'and' and 'the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisant means deferential, showing respect with a bow.

clue.text: Worker over the border in N Ireland

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A labourer crossing the border into Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' sets ANT above RIM. The definition names a place found in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Draughtsman gets back pay

indicators.note: back means the word is read the other way round

parts.note: a reward is payment for a service

explanation.surface: An architect's assistant receiving his wages owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who draws pictures or plans is a draughtsman.

clue.text: Greene's entertainment with internal letters?

parts.note: Graham Greene labelled some lighter novels entertainments; a seaside stick of rock has a resort name running through it

explanation.definitionFit: A Greene novel shares its name with a seaside candy stick lettered all through.

clue.text: An ancient section of a diagonal

indicators.note: a section of a word is a run of its letters lying inside it

explanation.surface: Part of an old diagonal line.
explanation.walkthrough: An ancient was an ensign, Iago's rank in Othello. 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Othello the villain holds the rank of ancient, an old word for ensign or standard-bearer.

clue.text: Common food of swallows

definitions.meaning: informal word for things to eat

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: grub in slang, and the verb meaning consumes.

clue.text: One who knocks off a crown?

definitions.text: One who knocks off a crown?

parts.words: One who knocks off a crown
parts.note: knocking off is killing, and the crown stands for the monarch

explanation.definitionFit: A king-killer kills a sovereign, the crown's wearer.

clue.text: Close to arena, where bookies stand with arrogance?

parts.note: the ring is the betting area at a racecourse where bookmakers take bets
side is an old word for swagger or pretension

explanation.surface: Bookmakers standing haughtily near the arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. Putting on side means acting superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringside seats are those right beside a boxing ring or circus arena.
